## Bottom line
**Suggests Benign (57%)** · Unreliable input · Careful review
Invasive risk is under 1%, but the input is flagged and Normal shares the conformal set [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Benign 57%, Normal 42% | Narrow lead |
| Conformal set | Normal, Benign (90%) | Cannot separate the two |
| Reliability / OOD | 70%; OOD 88th percentile | Flagged; input suspect |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Different top class |
| Similar cases | 2 of 5 Benign | Three of five Normal |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 7) · ↓ invasive · Score below typical; concept model leans away from invasive [F2] · Validated
- **Atypical cells confined within ducts** (region 1) · ↑ invasive · Typical score; spot check 12/20 [F3] · Weak
- **Marked nuclear pleomorphism** (region 9) · ↓ invasive · Low score; leans away from invasive · Validated
- **Frequent mitotic figures** (region 7) · ↓ invasive · Above-typical score, but spot check 0/20; disregard · Unreliable

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions cuts the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful.
- **Concepts**: Concept deletion minus random is 0.002 (CI −0.005 to 0.007): not shown to reflect the classifier. Mitoses (0/20) is Unreliable.

## Could be wrong if
- Image quality is flagged (OOD 88th percentile); a recut could shift the Benign versus Normal split.
- The second model picks a different top class, so the Benign lead is unstable.

## Check on the slide
1. **Region 7** — top region for infiltrating stroma and mitoses; confirm no invasive growth.
2. **Regions 8, 9** — highest heatmap contribution toward invasive; look for atypia or in situ change.
3. **Regions 1, 6** — top regions for duct-confined and benign-stroma concepts; judge Normal versus Benign.
